narr: Another active monsoon day impacted northern New Mexico on July 8, 2022, as thunderstorms developed across the mountainous terrain by early afternoon and becoming more widespread through the evening. Strong thunderstorms with heavy rainfall on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused Tecolote Creek to exceed its banks, flooding area roadways. Meanwhile, a thunderstorm near Raton interacted with a boundary to briefly produce quarter size hail.
ev: Heavy rain on Tecolote Creek on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon burn scar caused the creek to exceed its banks, flooding New Mexico State Road 283 and County Road A19A near Mineral Hill. Damages are estimated.
lsr: TECOLOTE CREEK EXCEEDING BANKS NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF NM STATE ROUTE 283 AND COUNTY ROAD A19A NEAR MINERAL HILL. WATER OVERFLOWING ONTO ROADS.
